questions.text: Which among the following is the correct full form of CCL (in terms of Banking)?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Cash Credit Limit.

Key Points

About CCL- Cash Credit Limit. 

  • It is a facility to withdraw money from a current bank account and do not need credit balance.
  • CCL is also limited to the extent of borrowing limit which is fixed by the commercial bank.
  • The interest on CCL is charged on the running balance and not the borrowing limit which is set by bank.
  • The short term loan taken by a borrower can only be extended upto  CCL of the account.
  • The borrowing limit is usually determined by the credit worthiness of the borrower.
  • It is also important to note that the interest charged is only on the running balance of the cash credit account and it is not on the total borrowing limit.

• CRISIL stands for Credit Rating and Information Service of India Limited.
  • It is a global company which provides ratings, research, and risk and policy advisory services.
  • India’s first MSE sentimental index for micro, small and medium enterprises, CriSidEx has been jointly developed by CRISIL and SIDBI.
  • It was launched by Finance minister Arun Jaitley.

questions.text: SWIFT is an _____ digit code and ‘I’ in SWIFT stands for ________.
questions.explanation:
SWIFT:

  • Stands for the “Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication”.
  • It is a standard identifier of a bank.
  • Is typically made up of 8 or 11 digits.
  • 8 digits code (without the branch code) denotes the primary office of the bank.

Example: HDFC IN BB DEL

First four letters

Denotes the name of the bank

HDFC

Denotes that the bank is “HDFC”

5th & 6th letters

Denotes the name of the country

IN

IN here stands for “INDIA”

7th & 8th letters

Tells about the location code about the bank

BB

Tells about the location of the bank

9th – 11th letters

Tells about the branch of the bank

DEL

Tells about the Delhi branch of this bank

questions.text: MIGA is an international financial institution which offers political risk insurance and credit enhancement guarantees. What is its full form?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency.

Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA)

  • The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency is an international institution that promotes investment in developing countries by offering political and economic risk insurance.
  • By promoting foreign direct investment into developing countries, the agency aims to support economic growth, reduce poverty, and improve people’s lives.
  • Understanding the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA)
  • The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group and is headquartered in Washington, D.C. As of March 2020, 181 member governments make up MIGA—156 developing nations and another 25 industrialized countries.

Core Banking Solutions (CBS):

questions.text: What is the full form of IMPS?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Immediate Payment Service.

Key Points 

  • IMPS is a real-time payment service.
  • IMPS is created by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
  • It empowers customers to transfer money instantly through banks and RBI authorized Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuers (PPI) across India.
  • The charges for transferring funds through IMPS are decided by the individual member banks and PPIs.
  • Benefits of IMPS:
    • Instant fund transfers.
    • Available 24 × 7 (functional even on holidays).
    • Safe and secure, easily accessible, and cost-effective.
    • Transactions from IMPS can be initiated through mobile/ internet / ATM channels.
    • Debit & Credit Confirmation by SMS.
  • NPCI:
    • It is an organization for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India.
    • It was established by RBI and the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA).
    • It is formed under the provisions of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
  • PPI: 
    • ​PPIs are instruments that facilitate purchasing goods and services, funds transfers, remittances, etc., against the value stored in/on such instruments.

questions.text: NEFT is the system in which the transactions received up to a particular time are processed in batches. What does NEFT stand for?
questions.explanation:
The Correct Answer is "National Electronic Funds Transfer".

Important Points

  • National Electronic Fund Transfer (NEFT) is a country-wide electronic fund transfer system for sending money from one bank account to another in a safe and hassle-free manner.
  • All NEFT settlements are made in a batch-wise format.
  • Money can be sent using this system to all NEFT-enabled banks in India on an individual basis.
  • To initiate an NEFT transfer, Bank IFSC Code is a must, along with other details such as bank account number, bank branch and account holder name, among other details.
  • Earlier, the NEFT transaction timings for most banks were between 8 a.m. And 6 p.m. from Monday to Friday and 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. on Saturdays.
  • However, with effect from 16 December 2019, you can transfer money via NEFT 24x7.
  • Money can be transferred via NEFT on holidays and weekends as well.

 

Key Points
The procedure for National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) is mentioned below:

  • Step 1: First login to your net banking account. If you do not have a net banking account then register for it on the website of your bank.
  • Step 2: Add the beneficiary as a payee. To do so, you have to enter the following details about the beneficiary in the ‘Add New Payee’ section:
    • Account Number.
    • Name.
    • IFSC Code.
    • Account Type.
  • Step 3: Once the payee is added, choose NEFT as a mode of Fund Transfer.
  • Step 4: Select the account you wish to transfer money from, the payee, enter the amount that you wish to transfer, and add remarks (optional).
  • Step 5: Click on submit.

questions.text: Expand the term INFINET in the context of banking and economy.
questions.explanation:
• INFINET stands for Indian Financial Network. 
  • It is a closed network consisting of the public and private sector organizations in the country engaged in the financial domain. 
  • It generally acts as the backbone of communication in the banking and financial sector of the country.
